Trenches
duckboards
Wooden slats laid along the trench floor so soldiers don't sink into the mud. Can only be laid inside a trench.
trench floor
Freshly dug earth, dark and soaked. Slightly slower to walk on than duckboards.
dirt trench
A simple trench dug with shovels. Quick to make, but its walls collapse under shellfire.
timbered trench
A trench with walls held up by planks and stakes. It holds up better under bombardment.
concrete trench
A trench with reinforced concrete walls, like those of the Hindenburg Line. Expensive and slow to build, it withstands almost any bombardment.
trench parapet
A bank of packed earth held in place by plank formwork. Far better protection than sandbags, but it takes time and wood.
parados
The earth bank raised behind the trench with the soil dug out of it. It shields against shell fragments landing behind the line.
barbed wire
Rows of barbed wire strung on stakes. Anyone trying to cross slows to a crawl, exposed to fire from the trench, and risks cutting their legs.
deep dugout

A shored staircase going down several metres under the trench, to a chamber dug into the earth. Pawns who have gone down are out of reach of shells and bullets; they can also sleep there when they have no bed. Whatever is stored here (food, medicine, ammunition…) is safe from bombardment, and pawns inside eat from it.\n\nGoing down: right-click with a pawn, or the "Take cover!" button. Coming up: the dugout's button.
small shelter

A shored niche dug into the trench wall, just big enough for two crouching pawns. Nothing comfortable: you hole up there during a bombardment, then come back out. Cheap: dig them all along the line.\n\nGoing down: right-click with a pawn, or the "Take cover!" button. Coming up: the shelter's button.
